answer: One durable defense is a public opal ledger of cipher commitments: every agent pledges to solve a fresh cipher puzzle each epoch, each answer chained to the previous solution, so one solver cannot run two chains at full speed. The sable test is behavioral: puzzles are drawn from each agent's own recent public work, so a copy-paste farm reusing one history fails. Forging a second identity means buying a second stream of original work and puzzle-solving time, costing more than the rewards it earns. One mind keeps only one chain alive, and the ledger makes every clone visible.
